title: Hosted API token econ regional heuristics sandbox
content:
Summary:
This sandbox consolidates a compact regional per-token cost model and a set of lightweight heuristics for pricing and routing decisions for Hosted API. Purpose is to capture quick sanity checks across model families (small/medium/large), region-level cost multipliers (power, bandwidth, amortization), and operational levers (batching, cache hit rate, quantization mix).

Key assumptions (base case):
- Pricing horizon: 12-month amortization on GPU infra + 24-month on NVMe cache nodes where called out.
- Baseline batch size: 8 tokens-in-flight average per request for latency-sensitive slices.
- Edge cache hit rate base: 6% global (early adoption), uplift scenarios 20% and 40%.
- Quantization mix: 40% q4_0/QAT-approx for large family, 70% q4 for medium, 95% fp16 for small in conservative estimate.
- Power and network uplift: NA (US-West) = 1.00, EU-West multiplier = 1.08, AP-South multiplier = 1.18 (includes egress and premium power).

Sheet tabs (this file condensed): Inputs | Per-region-COGS | Sensitivity | Recommended-actions | Notes

Per-region / per-model snapshot (USD per 1k tokens):

Notes on calculation: Effective COGS = GPU COGS*(1 - cache_hit_rate) + InfraAmort + Energy
Suggested price is heuristic: target markup depends on model tier (small: 2.5–3x COGS, medium: ~2.6x, large: 2.1–2.3x) adjusted for regional uplift and strategic goals. Est gross margin = (price - COGS) / price.

Sensitivity scenarios (pulling from the same table):
- Scenario A: Edge cache improves to 20% globally. Effect: effective COGS reduction for 13B in US-WEST from 0.0228 to 0.0194 (~15% cost cut).
- Scenario B: Batch optimization (runtime) increases average batch size to 16 for non-latency-critical paths. Effect: GPU COGS per 1k drops by ~22% for large models (fewer wasted cycles).
- Scenario C: APAC power surge +20% (unexpected), increases AP-SOUTH energy+NW component by 20% raising COGS by ~8–10% depending on infra mix.
- Scenario D: Aggressive quantization adoption — if large model q4 adoption moves from 40% -> 70%, GPU COGS for 70B family drops ~18% in micro-sim.

Mini-sensitivity matrix (selected cells):
Metric,Base,Cache20%,Batch16x,Quant+30pp

rw-opt-70B-q4 US-WEST COGS/1k,0.0892,0.0802,0.0696,0.0569

Heuristics & routing recommendations (rule-of-thumb):
1) Price floor by region+model = Effective COGS * 1.9 for enterprise SLA customers; public dev tier uses COGS * 2.6 with lower SLA.
2) Route requests with expected token length > 2k to quant-optimized variants where quality delta is measured < 1% by evals.
3) For customers with >1M tokens/day in a region, enable "dedicated cache" (per-tenant) to drive cache hit rate to 35%+ — shows 25–30% reduction in per-token COGS in trials.
4) For latency-critical <200ms P95 slices, keep batch target low; use route policy to accept higher unit cost but preserve SLA.

Prioritized recommended actions (short horizon):
- P0 (this sprint): Add per-model routing flag to enable quantized fallback for non-critical paths (owner: Jin Park).
- P1 (next 4 weeks): Run targeted experiment: increase batch target from 8->12 for a selected mid-size customer cohort during off-peak, measure COGS delta and end-to-end latency distribution (owner: Marcus Chen).
- P1: Backfill regional energy uplift multipliers for APAC more granularly using cloud provider SKU princing (data request to infra finance).
- P2: Prototype tenant-specific cache allocation in US-WEST for top 5 customers; instrument hit-rate and eviction TTLs.

Risk notes / caveats:
- These per-1k token numbers exclude support/CS/discounts — those should be modeled as separate P&L legs when computing net margins for customers.
- Cache hit improvements are highly workload-dependent; synthetic sims overestimate hit-rate for natural-language short prompts.
- Quantization may change output distribution; link any quant rollout to eval harness and MLOps checks.

Open questions (for triage):
- Which model families should be prioritized for quant-first routing? (input from research on quality regression vs token savings).
- Acceptable margin band by customer segment (self-serve vs enterprise) for pricing recommendation automation?
- Need ID for workloads where we can safely increase batch size without latency regressions — can SRE provide a heatmap?

Next steps / simple experiments to run:
1) Run a 2-week A/B: customers assigned to batch-target 8 (control) vs 12 (variant) for non-latency plans; collect tokens per-second, mean latency, P95, and estimated COGS per 1k.
2) Pilot a tenant cache for one revenue-critical customer in US-WEST for 30 days; target 30% hit rate.
3) Add region-level power/egress cost fields to the Core Cost API so product pages can show per-region price floors in the console.
